title: DISTRIBUTED CACHE
subtitle: Design Redis itself: data structures inside one node, then distribution across many.
footer: DDIA: Ch 6 consistent hashing · Ch 5 async replication   ·   Similar: URL shortener · Rate limiter · Business discovery · News feed

items: One node is a hash map plus a doubly linked list for O(1) least-recently-used eviction.
Spread keys with consistent hashing and virtual nodes, so adding a node moves only a small share of keys.
Replicate asynchronously for failover, and spread hot keys over several nodes.
Each node handles ≫ 100k ops/s, so memory, not CPU, sets the node count.

blocks.text: One node: a HashMap for O(1) lookup plus a doubly linked list for LRU order (move to head on access, evict the tail). TTL by lazy check plus a background sweep.

items: Shard across nodes with consistent hashing (with virtual nodes). The client computes the owner directly, so there is no extra hop.
Each primary replicates asynchronously to a replica; on failure the replica is promoted.
Ring membership lives in a config service; clients watch it. Hot keys get replicated across several nodes or a short-TTL local cache.
HashMap → linked-list node; get = move to head; evict = remove tail.
Consistent hashing moves ~1/N of keys; vnodes keep load even; warm gradually.
Copies key#0..k on several nodes with random reads, or a client-side L1 cache.
Every scale event remaps ~all keys, and the cold cache stampedes the database.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
